checks.title: GuardDuty is active in every region with resources (regions with no resources and no detector are reported with low severity)

verify.pass_when_text: Each region with resources has a GuardDuty detector with Status=ENABLED. A region with no resources and no detector does not break the Drata test, but it is reported with low severity: an attacker can use regions without monitoring. Accounts with S3 buckets count us-east-1 as a region with resources.

steps: Enable GuardDuty in region {region} with S3 Protection turned on, running the command in that region.
If the region already has a detector (for example a disabled one), the command re-enables it with update-detector instead of creating another one.
Verify with get-detector that Status is ENABLED.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
# creates the detector; if the region already has one (for example a disabled one), it re-enables it with S3 Protection
DETECTOR_ID=$(aws guardduty list-detectors --region "$REGION" --query 'DetectorIds[0]' --output text) || DETECTOR_ID="READ_FAILED"
if [ "$DETECTOR_ID" = "READ_FAILED" ]; then echo "STOPPED: could not list the GuardDuty detectors (guardduty:ListDetectors); nothing was changed"; elif [ -z "$DETECTOR_ID" ] || [ "$DETECTOR_ID" = "None" ]; then aws guardduty create-detector --enable --region "$REGION" --features '[{"Name":"S3_DATA_EVENTS","Status":"ENABLED"}]'; else aws guardduty update-detector --detector-id "$DETECTOR_ID" --enable --features '[{"Name":"S3_DATA_EVENTS","Status":"ENABLED"}]' --region "$REGION"; fi
remediation.verify_after: aws guardduty get-detector --detector-id "$(aws guardduty list-detectors --region "{region}" --query 'DetectorIds[0]' --output text)" --region "{region}" --query '{Status: Status, S3: Features[?Name==`S3_DATA_EVENTS`].Status | [0]}'
remediation.notes: No downtime. Cost: 30-day free trial and then GuardDuty charges by volume of analyzed events (CloudTrail, flow logs, DNS and, with S3 Protection, S3 data events); in a region with no activity the cost is minimal. Findings from regions with no resources have low severity: enabling them anyway closes the gap of unmonitored regions that the AWS security baseline recommends. The detector is per region: repeat the command in each offending region.

checks.title: GuardDuty has S3 Protection enabled (if the account has S3 buckets)

verify.pass_when_text: Every enabled detector has S3_DATA_EVENTS=ENABLED. If the account has no S3 buckets it passes, like Drata test 105. With no enabled detector at all it fails: there is no S3 Protection.

steps: Turn on S3 Protection on the GuardDuty detector in region {region}.
If the region has no enabled detector, the finding is resolved with the DET-001 command, which already creates it with S3 Protection.
Verify with get-detector that S3_DATA_EVENTS is ENABLED.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
DETECTOR_ID=$(aws guardduty list-detectors --region "$REGION" --query 'DetectorIds[0]' --output text) && aws guardduty update-detector --detector-id "$DETECTOR_ID" --features '[{"Name":"S3_DATA_EVENTS","Status":"ENABLED"}]' --region "$REGION"
remediation.verify_after: aws guardduty get-detector --detector-id "$(aws guardduty list-detectors --region "{region}" --query 'DetectorIds[0]' --output text)" --region "{region}" --query 'Features[?Name==`S3_DATA_EVENTS`]'
remediation.notes: No downtime. Cost: GuardDuty charges S3 Protection per million S3 data events analyzed; on buckets with heavy object traffic it can be significant. Drata 105 requires S3 Protection together with GuardDuty active in the regions with resources.

checks.title: An EventBridge rule exists for GuardDuty findings with at least one target

verify.pass_when_text: At least one region has an enabled EventBridge rule, on the default bus, whose pattern selects source aws.guardduty (and detail-type GuardDuty Finding if it declares one) and that has at least one target. Patterns with operators that are not modeled (prefix, etc.) do not count.

steps: Decide the destination of the findings (an SNS topic with real subscribers, a Lambda to the team chat, a ticketing tool) and allow events.amazonaws.com to publish in its policy.
Create the EventBridge rule for GuardDuty findings and add the target to it.
Confirm that the target receives a test finding (GuardDuty sample findings).
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
RULE_NAME="guardduty-findings"
SNS_TOPIC_ARN="__FILL_IN_SNS_TOPIC_ARN__"
aws events put-rule --name "$RULE_NAME" --event-pattern '{"source":["aws.guardduty"],"detail-type":["GuardDuty Finding"]}' --state ENABLED --region "$REGION" && aws events put-targets --rule "$RULE_NAME" --targets "Id=notify,Arn=$SNS_TOPIC_ARN" --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: Decision: SNS topic or another target, and which severity to notify (the pattern can filter on detail.severity to receive only HIGH and CRITICAL). The SNS topic policy must allow sns:Publish to events.amazonaws.com or the events are lost with no visible error; the email subscription notice must be confirmed. If a rule with another name and no target already exists, put-targets on it is enough. Negligible cost. It must be repeated in each region with GuardDuty if you want alerts in all of them. It is part of the how-to for Drata test 105, although Drata does not evaluate it.

checks.title: Security Hub is enabled with the FSBP or CIS standard

verify.pass_when_text: Each region with resources has Security Hub enabled with AWS Foundational Security Best Practices or CIS AWS Foundations in READY state. Other standards alone (PCI DSS) are not enough; Security Hub turned off is a failure.

steps: Enable Security Hub in region {region} without the default standards (if it was already enabled, the command leaves it as it is) and enable FSBP.
Wait a few minutes and verify that the standard moves to READY.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
# if Security Hub is already enabled in the region it only enables the standard; if not, it enables it first (and the standard is enabled only if that succeeded)
if aws securityhub describe-hub --region "$REGION" > /dev/null 2>&1; then HUB_READY=1; else aws securityhub enable-security-hub --no-enable-default-standards --region "$REGION" && HUB_READY=1; fi
[ "$HUB_READY" = "1" ] && aws securityhub batch-enable-standards --standards-subscription-requests '[{"StandardsArn":"arn:aws:securityhub:{region}::standards/aws-foundational-security-best-practices/v/1.0.0"}]' --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: No downtime. Security Hub controls depend on AWS Config with the recorder active (see DET-005): without it, the controls have no data. Cost: charged per security check run and per ingested finding, with a 30-day trial. To add CIS in addition to FSBP, also enable its standard. It must be repeated in every region with resources; cross-region aggregation is optional and is not evaluated by this check.

checks.title: AWS Config is enabled in all regions: recording, all resource types, IAM daily and with a delivery channel

verify.pass_when_text: Each enabled region has an AWS Config recorder with recording=true, without a last status of FAILURE, that records all resource types, with the global IAM types (User, Role, Group, Policy) at DAILY frequency, and a delivery channel with an S3 bucket.

vanta.test: AWS Config is enabled in all regions
AWS Config is enabled correctly in all regions

steps: Decide the S3 bucket that receives the Config data (a dedicated bucket, with the bucket policy that allows config.amazonaws.com to write) and, if desired, an SNS topic for changes.
Create the Config service-linked role if it does not exist.
Create the recorder in region {region} with all resource types and the global IAM types at DAILY, create the delivery channel and start the recorder.
Verify with describe-configuration-recorder-status that recording is true.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
# create-service-linked-role fails if the role already exists: that is expected
aws iam create-service-linked-role --aws-service-name config.amazonaws.com

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
CONFIG_BUCKET="__FILL_IN_CONFIG_BUCKET__"
CONFIG_ROLE_ARN="arn:aws:iam::$ACCOUNT_ID:role/aws-service-role/config.amazonaws.com/AWSServiceRoleForConfig"
# the recorder only starts if the recorder and the delivery channel were created
CHANNELS=$(aws configservice describe-delivery-channels --region "$REGION" --query 'length(DeliveryChannels)' --output text)
# if the region already has a delivery channel (or it could not be read), it does nothing: put-delivery-channel would replace it and divert Config delivery
if [ "$CHANNELS" != "0" ]; then echo "STOPPED: the region already has a delivery channel (or it could not be read): put-delivery-channel would replace it; review describe-delivery-channels and describe-configuration-recorders before continuing"; else aws configservice put-configuration-recorder --configuration-recorder "{\"name\":\"default\",\"roleARN\":\"$CONFIG_ROLE_ARN\",\"recordingGroup\":{\"allSupported\":true,\"includeGlobalResourceTypes\":true},\"recordingMode\":{\"recordingFrequency\":\"CONTINUOUS\",\"recordingModeOverrides\":[{\"description\":\"IAM global types daily\",\"resourceTypes\":[\"AWS::IAM::User\",\"AWS::IAM::Role\",\"AWS::IAM::Group\",\"AWS::IAM::Policy\"],\"recordingFrequency\":\"DAILY\"}]}}" --region "$REGION" && aws configservice put-delivery-channel --delivery-channel "name=default,s3BucketName=$CONFIG_BUCKET" --region "$REGION" && aws configservice start-configuration-recorder --configuration-recorder-name default --region "$REGION"; fi

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
RECORDER_NAME="default"
# only if the recorder already exists but is stopped
aws configservice start-configuration-recorder --configuration-recorder-name "$RECORDER_NAME" --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: No downtime. Cost: AWS Config charges per configuration item recorded and per rule evaluation; recording the global IAM types in each region at DAILY frequency (instead of continuous) is what Vanta asks for so as not to multiply that cost. It must be repeated in every enabled region. If the region already has a recorder with another name, put-configuration-recorder with that name updates it; there can be only one recorder and one delivery channel per region. Caution: put-configuration-recorder with the name default replaces the settings of an existing recorder with that name, and put-delivery-channel replaces the existing delivery channel (it would redirect Config delivery, for example away from the organization's aggregation bucket): that is why the second block stops with STOPPED if the region already has a delivery channel; in that case review what exists and, if only the recorder needs to be started, use the third block. Vanta also expects an SNS topic on the delivery channel (snsTopicARN=... in put-delivery-channel); this check does not fail for that. Decision: destination bucket and SNS topic.

checks.title: Inspector is active for EC2, ECR and Lambda

verify.pass_when_text: In each region with resources, Inspector has EC2, ECR and Lambda (standard) scanning ENABLED. A state of ENABLING does not count yet; Inspector turned off is a failure.

vanta.test: Critical vulnerabilities identified in packages are addressed (AWS Inspector)

steps: Turn on Inspector for EC2, ECR and Lambda in region {region}.
Verify with batch-get-account-status that the three types are ENABLED.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
aws inspector2 enable --resource-types EC2 ECR LAMBDA --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: No downtime. Cost: Inspector charges per scanned EC2 instance, per ECR image (on push and on each re-scan) and per Lambda function, with a 15-day trial. Agent-based EC2 scanning needs the instance to be managed by Systems Manager (see CMP-006). Security Hub controls Inspector.3 and .4 additionally ask for Lambda code scanning, which this check does not require. Vanta takes the Inspector and ECR findings for its critical vulnerabilities test; the SLA is configured in the Vanta app.

checks.title: There are no open CRITICAL or HIGH findings in Inspector

verify.offenders: findings[].{resource_id: resources[0].id, detail: {severity: severity, title: title, vulnerability: packageVulnerabilityDetails.vulnerabilityId}}
verify.pass_when_text: Inspector has no findings in ACTIVE state with CRITICAL or HIGH severity. The first 100 findings per region are read: enough to decide whether the check fails, not to count them all. Any open finding of that severity fails, regardless of its age; the remediation SLA is defined by each tool.

vanta.test: Critical vulnerabilities identified in packages are addressed (AWS Inspector)

steps: List the open CRITICAL and HIGH findings and group them by resource and by package or image.

Fix them according to the resource type: patch EC2 instances with Patch Manager in an agreed window; update the package or base image of the containers, rebuild and publish the image; update the dependency of the Lambda functions and redeploy them.
If a finding cannot be fixed, document the exception with an owner and a review date and suppress it with an Inspector filter.
Wait for the re-scan (Inspector closes only the fixed findings) and verify that none remain open.
commands:
REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
aws inspector2 list-findings --filter-criteria '{"findingStatus":[{"comparison":"EQUALS","value":"ACTIVE"}],"severity":[{"comparison":"EQUALS","value":"CRITICAL"},{"comparison":"EQUALS","value":"HIGH"}]}' --region "$REGION" --query 'findings[].[severity,resources[0].id,title]' --output table

REGION="{region}"
ACCOUNT_ID="{account_id}"
INSTANCE_ID="{resource_id}"
# only if the finding's resource is an EC2 instance
# NoReboot: kernel patches remain pending until the next reboot
aws ssm send-command --document-name "AWS-RunPatchBaseline" --parameters 'Operation=Install,RebootOption=NoReboot' --targets "Key=instanceids,Values=$INSTANCE_ID" --region "$REGION"
remediation.notes: Patching changes the software in production: test first in a non-production environment. With RebootOption=RebootIfNeeded the patching reboots the instance (downtime if there is no redundancy); with NoReboot kernel patches are not applied until the next reboot. Findings for ECR images and Lambda are not resolved by patching the resource live: they require rebuilding and deploying. A suppressed finding stops counting, but you must be able to justify it to the auditor. Remediation SLAs are set by each tool (Vanta: Settings > Vulnerability remediation SLAs; Drata does not publish them).
